# Security Requirements Checklist: OAuth API Security

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurability of OAuth/OIDC authorization and API-wide bypass requirements before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-10-22
**Feature**: [OAuth API Security specification](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Authorization Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are credential-validation requirements specified for every mapped API endpoint when standard mode is active? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Are issuer, audience, expiry, and scope requirements all specified as independent conditions for accepting a caller credential? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK003 Are administrator and reader authorization requirements defined for every endpoint classification? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the reader-accessible endpoint set explicitly defined as all HTTP GET endpoints plus the two named authentication routes? [Completeness, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK005 Are authorization requirements for future mapped controller endpoints documented rather than inferred from the current controller inventory? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Spec §Assumptions]

## Authorization Requirement Clarity and Consistency

- [ ] CHK006 Is the term "reader-accessible endpoint" used consistently across the user stories, functional requirements, key entities, and assumptions? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 2, Spec §FR-004, Spec §Key Entities, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the distinction between a reader-only caller and a caller holding both reader and administrator scopes unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 2, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the two named reader-accessible authentication routes identified with enough path detail to distinguish them from any other authentication operations? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK009 Are the administrator-only requirements for all other non-GET endpoints consistent with the explicitly permitted reader-accessible POST routes? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-004]

## Bypass Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK010 Is the default-disabled behavior specified both for an omitted bypass setting and for an explicitly false setting? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK011 Are bypass-mode requirements explicit that missing, invalid, expired, wrong-authority, wrong-resource, and insufficient-scope credentials do not cause authorization denial? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the configuration values required in standard mode and permitted to be absent in bypass mode fully enumerated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-008a]
- [ ] CHK013 Is production use of the bypass explicitly documented as a deliberate trust decision rather than an implied environment exception? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007a, Spec §Assumptions]

## Bypass Safety and Exception Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 Are the safeguards that remain active in bypass mode—input validation, directory safety checks, business rules, and safe errors—explicitly distinguished from OAuth/OIDC checks? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements defined for returning from bypass mode to standard mode, including restoration of administrator and reader authorization rules? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements defined for active-mode diagnostics that identify bypass state without disclosing credentials, secrets, or authority internals? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the operational meaning of a "valid bypass setting" sufficiently specified for absent, malformed, and conflicting configuration scenarios? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-008a]

## Acceptance-Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK018 Can the 100% authorization-denial requirement be objectively measured against a complete definition of the API endpoint inventory? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK019 Can the 100% bypass-access requirement be objectively measured while distinguishing authorization access from downstream validation or business-rule outcomes? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK020 Are configuration-startup failure and bypass-startup success criteria specific enough to distinguish missing, blank, malformed, and conflicting values? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-005, Spec §SC-005a]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK021 Is the authority's responsibility for issuing scopes and the API resource audience documented as an external dependency with clear assumptions? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements explicit about the authority-metadata transport requirement and the security consequence of its configured value? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-008]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
